I am getting ready for this season. I have 9 mu altogether. I will split it — 4 mu for cotton and 5 mu for spring maize, same as last year because that worked fine and my husband already bought some seed.

For the spring maize, I plant at the end of April after the soil warms. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed — everyone around me plants it and the yield is steady. Last year I got about 580 kg per mu, so I aim for 600 this year. I spread compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base, about 50 kg per mu when I plough, then top-dress with urea at the big trumpet stage, maybe 25 kg per mu. That gives me around 22 kg of nitrogen, which is what my neighbors use too. Phosphorus and potassium I don't worry about much — what's in the compound is enough. I irrigate from the well 3 times — once before planting, once at jointing, once at grain filling. Pesticide twice is enough, one for armyworm and one for corn borer.

For cotton, I plant mid-April under plastic film. I buy Bt hybrid seed from the dealer in town — it saves me spraying for bollworm. Cotton eats a lot of nitrogen but too much makes it grow tall with few bolls, so I use about 18 kg N per mu, split between base and flowering. Potassium matters for bolls so I add a bag of potassium sulfate, maybe 10 kg K per mu. Cotton needs water at flowering, I irrigate 3 times. Even with Bt, I still spray 5 times for aphids, mites, and the bollworm that slips through. Last year I picked 280 kg per mu, I hope for the same.

I plough both fields before planting — rotary is not deep enough for cotton roots, and I have always ploughed.
